claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A limited set of targeted DFT calculations can capture the relevant local and interfacial electronic and structural features.
Mesoscale descriptors can represent variability in the hierarchical heterostructure.
Physics-based alloy features can capture composition-dependent behavior and support generalization to previously unseen high-entropy alloys.
The proposed transfer-learning model will accurately predict Young's modulus of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed transfer-learning model will accurately predict yield strength of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed transfer-learning model will accurately predict tensile toughness of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Combining targeted DFT with machine learning can reduce computational cost relative to applying DFT to every candidate configuration.
Multilevel structural and chemical-ordering descriptors link local electronic properties to macroscopic mechanical performance.
Transferring DFT-derived information through mesoscale descriptors will preserve first-principles accuracy while improving computational efficiency.
The method is reliable only when its descriptors capture the dominant variations in local chemical order and phase heterogeneity.
The initial DFT sample must sufficiently span the relevant configurational space.
The proposed model will reduce RMSE for Young's modulus, yield strength, and tensile toughness by approximately 30% relative to standard machine learning based only on lower-fidelity features.
The proposed model will be approximately 1000 times more computationally efficient than exhaustive DFT or high-throughput atomistic simulation.
Physically based yield-strength calculations can be complicated and lengthy, making surrogate models easier to apply to thousands of alloys.
Conventional machine-learning methods are less effective at capturing the hierarchical structural complexity of HfNbTiVAl10.
Unrepresented abrupt chemical-ordering changes or unforeseen phase transitions would make the framework unreliable.
Significant deviations from the nominal composition or assumed processing conditions would degrade prediction accuracy.
Related studies provide preliminary support for improved predictive accuracy and efficiency.

contradictions.description: The prediction target is called tensile toughness in the hypothesis and outcome, fracture toughness in the test design, and 'tensile toughness/fracture energy' in the measurements. These are distinct mechanical quantities and are not defined as interchangeable.
